Fit a latent class model that groups observations by their pattern of categorical responses

Source: R/lpa.R
lca.Rd

lca() fits a latent class model, which describes heterogeneity in categorical response patterns through a specified number of latent classes. Each class is characterized by the probabilities of the response categories for each indicator, which describe how response patterns differ between classes.

lca() estimates the class-specific response probabilities and class proportions, together with posterior membership probabilities for each observation. Indicators are assumed independent conditional on class membership unless associations between selected indicators are explicitly specified. The posterior probabilities describe uncertainty in classification; an observation's assigned class is a summary of these probabilities.

The model treats observations as independent. For observations nested within groups, use multilca(). Ordinal and count indicators can also be fitted using the structured measurement models described in multilpa().

Usage

lca(data, vars, n_classes, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per observation.

vars

Names of the discrete indicator columns. Numeric, integer, logical, character and factor columns are accepted, and every distinct value of a column is one category. Columns named in ordinal or count (through ...) are modelled as such; the rest are categorical.

n_classes

Number of classes; a positive integer.

...

Further arguments, passed through multilca() to multilpa(), which documents all of them. The ones used most often:

  • missing: "error" (default) stops when an indicator has a missing value; "fiml" keeps every row and uses the responses it has.

  • ordinal, count: indicators in vars modelled as ordered categories or as counts instead of as unordered categories.

  • local_dependence: pairs of indicators, written "item1:item2", that stay associated within a class.

  • n_starts (default 10) and seed: the number of starts and the seed that makes them reproducible.

  • min_probability: the lower bound on a response probability (default 1e-10).

  • profile_covariates: covariates that predict class membership.

id and n_group_classes are not accepted (they belong to the two-level model), and neither is n_profiles: the number of classes is n_classes.

Value

A fitted model of class multilpa, or multilpa_covariates when profile_covariates is given. The classes are numbered 1, 2, and so on in the profile column of its tables. get_results() returns the tables by name, among them:

  • "responses" (also as.data.frame(fit)): one row per class, indicator and category, with the response probability and its standard error;

  • "profile_probabilities": the proportion of each class;

  • "assignments": the data with each row's most likely class and its posterior probabilities;

  • "classification" and "entropy": how clearly the rows are classified;

  • "residuals": bivariate residuals, which show pairs of indicators the classes do not explain;

  • "information_criteria" and "starts".

The fit's call records the original lca() call.

Conditions

Errors: latents_bad_argument when id, n_group_classes or n_profiles is passed; latents_bad_data when a column is missing from data or an indicator has missing values under missing = "error"; latents_bad_categorical when categorical names a column not in vars. Warnings: latents_unidentified when the model has more free parameters than the table of response patterns has free cells, latents_unconverged when the reported start did not converge, and latents_small_classes when a class is nearly empty. multilpa() raises the others, and latents-conditions lists them all.

See also

lpa() for continuous indicators; multilca() for the two-level model; enumerate_lca() to compare numbers of classes.

Examples

fit <- lca(student_esm, c("time_with_friends", "on_social_media",
                          "tv_video_games", "sports"),
           n_classes = 2, n_starts = 3, seed = 1)
fit
#> Latent class analysis: 2 classes
#> 2582 observations; 4 categorical indicators
#> Classes are labelled profile_1, profile_2, ... in every table.
#> Log likelihood: -4560.239231 | AIC: 9138.478 | BIC: 9191.185
#> Converged: TRUE | iterations: 69 | best log likelihood reached by 3 of 3 starts (3 converged)
#> 
#> Class sizes   profile_1 35.6% (919)   profile_2 64.4% (1663)
#> 
#> Response probabilities
#>          indicator category profile_1 profile_2
#>  time_with_friends       no     0.782     0.897
#>  time_with_friends      yes     0.218     0.103
#>    on_social_media       no     1.000     0.552
#>    on_social_media      yes     0.000     0.448
#>     tv_video_games       no     1.000     0.670
#>     tv_video_games      yes     0.000     0.330
#>             sports       no     0.902     0.943
#>             sports      yes     0.098     0.057
#> 
#> Thresholds and standard errors: get_results(x, "responses").
#> Every other table: get_results(x, what = ), or get_results(x, "all").
get_results(fit, "profile_probabilities")
#>   group_class profile probability group_class_probability
#> 1           1       1   0.3557785                       1
#> 2           1       2   0.6442215                       1
plot(fit, what = "heatmap")
